definitions.explanation: A humble expression for reading something written by a respected person. Used when referring to reading someone else's writing with respect.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}のご{著書|ちょしょ}を{拝読|はいどく}いたしました。
examples.notes: Humble form when speaking to the author

examples.japanese: お{手紙|てがみ}{拝読|はいどく}しました。
{記事|きじ}を{拝読|はいどく}し、{大変|たいへん}{感銘|かんめい}を{受|う}けました。
examples.english: I read your article and was deeply impressed.

examples.japanese: メールを{拝読|はいどく}いたしました。

notes:
KEIGO ({敬語|けいご}): {謙譲語|けんじょうご} (humble language). The prefix {拝|はい} indicates humble respect toward the person whose writing is being read.

VERB FORM:
・{拝読|はいどく}する (to read - humble)
・{拝読|はいどく}いたす (more formal humble form)

CONTEXTS: Used in formal business correspondence, academic settings, and when addressing respected figures.

RELATED {拝|はい} COMPOUNDS:
・{拝見|はいけん} (to see/look at - humble)
・{拝聴|はいちょう} (to listen - humble)
・{拝借|はいしゃく} (to borrow - humble)
・{拝受|はいじゅ} (to receive - humble)

PLAIN EQUIVALENT: {読|よ}む (to read - neutral)
